_comment: Copy to config.json and edit. config.json is gitignored: it holds your API keys.
_manifest_comment: Where to remember how much of each conversation has already been turned into a post. This is what makes the run incremental instead of date-based; see the README. Delete the file to start over.
_persona_comment: The single most important setting. Describe WHO reads you and what your project is, in plain words. Without it the drafts drift into engineering changelogs.
persona:
Write for a smart reader who is NOT a developer: a founder, a marketer, someone building a business. They understand 'server', 'bug', 'backup'. They do not know and will scroll past ACL, POSIX, commit, repo, staging. Say what a thing MEANT, not what it was called. Technical words are seasoning, not the meal: one or two per post at most.

My project: <one or two sentences about what you are building, so the post can name it accurately>.

I work alone. I may work on several different projects, so check what the facts are actually about before attributing the work to any one of them.
_translate_comment: Leave translate_to empty for a single language. Set it to post the same content to a second audience; it is a translation of the approved post, not a second draft, so both audiences read the same story.
_keys_comment: Only fill in the ones you have. Missing providers are skipped, and the cascade uses whatever is left. All four have a free tier and none needs a credit card.
_telegram_comment: Optional. Without it, drafts print to stdout. A private channel is a good inbox: it reaches your phone and nothing is public until you copy it out.
_rules_comment: Mechanical checks. Every one exists because a model broke it in testing. preview_chars is the one that matters most: the X timeline only shows the first ~280 characters.
